parties.respondent: The State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors.

summary: The appeal challenges the Madhya Pradesh High Court's judgment denying regular pay scale to appellant employees appointed as 'part-time sweepers' under a Special Recruitment Drive. The High Court had relied on its earlier decision in Ram Naresh Prajapati vs State of M.P., where employees appointed under similar conditions were granted regular pay scale after three years under circular dated 10.05.1984. The appellants, appointed between 2005–2007 under the same drive and selection process, sought parity. The key issue was whether they were entitled to regular pay scale under the 1984 circular and subsequent administrative orders, despite being designated 'part-time'. The Supreme Court examined the applicability of the circular, the nature of their appointment, and the principle of equal treatment. It considered whether the High Court erred in distinguishing their case from Ram Naresh Prajapati, and whether the state's refusal violated principles of fairness and due process.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 309 of the Constitution of India
